item.title: Stronger Montclair: An Introduction to the Strong Towns Movement — Thu Sep 17, 6:00 PM — Montclair Main - Auditorium
item.description:
What does it take to make Montclair a great place to live while remaining financially sustainable?
Join us for an introduction to the Strong Towns movement and explore how its ideas can help Montclair build a stronger, more resilient future. We’ll examine the challenges of suburban development, municipal finances, housing, transportation, parking, and land use—and discuss practical principles for creating a prosperous community at a human scale.
The program will conclude with a discussion of next steps for Montclair residents and how we can work together to build a stronger town.
Come learn, ask questions, and explore what Strong Towns could mean for Montclair.
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.title: AEW: SKILLS IN ACTION 2026 — Thu Sep 24, 12:00 PM — Cole Hall 340 (Third Floor)
item.description:
Wondering how your strengths can shape your future? This interactive workshop will help you discover and build on the skills that matter most to you. In this session, you’ll: Identify your skills and strengths through self-assessment. Determine how those skills connect to possible majors and career paths. Create an action plan to grow your skills using the Discovery Program's AI-powered Major Mentor. Additionally, Major Mentor will help you map majors that align with your strengths and provide real next steps. Skills in Action: Mapping Your Strengths to Majors is part of Academic Exploration Week, a longstanding immersive experience presented by The Discovery Program. To contact the Discovery Program, email us at discoveryprogram@montclair.edu, or visit us at montclair.edu/discovery-program.
Hosted by: The Discovery Program

item.description:
A book club for adults who want to read in community. We meet one Friday morning a month to chat about a title we read in common.
-- Back to School September: Reading the Classics
SULA by Toni Morrison (1973)
A modern masterpiece about love and kinship, about living in an America birthed from slavery. Nobel Prize laureate Toni Morrison gives life to characters who struggle with what society tells them to be, and the love they long for and crave as Black women. (from the publisher)
--
Reading club participants are also encouraged to read the chapter on Sula (pp 49-70) in:
ON MORRISON by Namwali Serpell (2026) **pages 49-70 only

How to support your child's reading at home Review your child's current reading assessment (please bring copies, if possible) Learn what resources we have at the library to check out for your developing or struggling reader Other areas of concern or curiosity regarding your child's literacy development
